I started running last year and told myself I’d run at least 3 times a week. 

But I’d get SO upset whenever I couldn’t get a “proper” run in. Because I ended work late, had other commitments, just didn’t feel like it, etc. 

Then I started telling myself that on those days, all I had to do was a “minimum” run. And that’s where this idea of a Minimum Viable Action started for me. 

So as we Rethink Healthy, here’s a lil reminder to free yourself of the idea that you need to optimise every little thing. Esp when you end up sweating the small stuff and losing sight of what actually matters…for your health and your life.

Sometimes, small, sustainable actions that you can keep coming back to can get you further than big, audacious goals that don’t always fit into real life.

So on the days when life just feels like A LOT, what’s your minimum viable action? 👇

transcript.text: In a world where we're all taught to constantly optimize our health, our protein, our workouts,
our sleep, our hormones, I took a moment to rethink healthy and I actually think we can
all benefit from optimizing just a little less.
So I want to share with you something I've been practicing myself, which is health deoptimization.
Because somewhere along the way, being healthy became pretty complicated.
There's always another wearable to get, another metric to track, another habit to keep up
with.
And while some of these things can be useful, I don't think every part of our health needs
to be optimized, especially when it starts causing stress or distracting us from the foundations
that actually matter to our health.
So during particularly busy, stressful or overstretched periods, instead of trying to keep up with
everything I'm supposed to do for my health, I simply ask myself, what's the smallest thing
I can realistically do today?
I call this my minimum viable action.
So let me give you a couple of examples.
Say I've had a less than ideal meal.
I don't fuss about trying to make up for it.
Maybe my minimum is simply having a fruit when I get home.
